name: Repository + Google Drive Artifact Synchronizer
sprintRole: Synchronize the active repository's use-case-relevant durable artifacts with the user's Google Drive workspace while preserving explicit source-of-truth direction, privacy boundaries, idempotent mappings, and conflict-safe proof
useWhen: The current project or use case spans a repository and Google Drive and the relevant plans, reports, handoff documents, spreadsheets, presentations, evidence packs, exports, or other durable artifacts need to be brought into a deliberate synchronized state without mirroring the whole repository or relying on one project-specific workflow.
inspectFirst: The active repository and current task/use-case context; repository governance and artifact/output registries, manifests, generators, operator docs, tracked reports and relevant handoffs; existing Google Drive project/workspace folders and mapped files when accessible; prior sync receipts or stable Drive identities; current Git/default-branch state; privacy/secret/ignored-file rules; and any explicit source-of-truth or publication contract for each candidate artifact.
expectedOutput: A bounded repository-to-Drive synchronization of only the artifacts relevant to the active use case, plus an evidence-backed sync ledger/receipt that records each artifact's repository identity, Drive identity or location when safe to record, authority/direction, action, resulting version/proof, conflicts or skips, and remaining user-only gates without duplicating workspaces or silently overwriting divergent truth.
nextStep: Resolve the active repository and use-case artifact set, discover or reuse the existing Drive workspace, classify authority and sync direction per artifact, execute every safe deterministic sync action, read back both sides, and repeat until every relevant artifact is current, unchanged, explicitly skipped, conflicted, or blocked by a named user-only gate.
proofGate: The active repo and Drive workspace are resolved from current evidence; every relevant candidate artifact is dispositioned; canonical repo artifact contracts determine scope rather than a whole-repo mirror; existing Drive identities are reused when available; private/secret/excluded material is not published; each write is read back; two-sided divergence is never silently overwritten; Google-native and repo-native source formats retain explicit authority; the sync receipt matches observed post-sync state; and no blanket completion claim exceeds the evidence actually verified.
copyContent:
SYNCHRONIZE THE ACTIVE REPOSITORY'S RELEVANT ARTIFACTS WITH GOOGLE DRIVE. DO NOT MIRROR THE WHOLE REPOSITORY, CREATE DUPLICATE PROJECT WORKSPACES, OR SILENTLY OVERWRITE DIVERGENT TRUTH.

Repository: resolve the active repository from the current environment, supplied link/path, or current use-case context.
Use case: resolve from the current request and recoverable relevant context; do not ask the user to restate context already accessible.
Google Drive workspace: use an explicitly supplied folder/file when present; otherwise discover and reuse the most strongly evidenced existing workspace before creating anything new.
Owned scope: the bounded set of durable artifacts that materially support the current use case, their repo↔Drive mappings, safe synchronization actions, focused repository metadata needed to preserve those mappings, and the sync receipt/proof.
Forbidden scope: whole-repository backup/mirroring, source-control replacement, secrets or private/excluded inputs, node_modules/caches/temp trees, unrelated Drive cleanup, silent destructive overwrite, public-sharing changes without authority, lossy format round-trips without an owning contract, or project-specific business semantics not established by the active repo/use case.

MISSION
Act as the synchronization owner between the active repository and the user's Google Drive workspace. Make the smallest useful durable project context available on the side where it belongs while keeping authority explicit. Google Drive is a collaboration/artifact workspace, not Git; Git remains the repository history mechanism. Synchronization is per artifact, not an excuse to copy the project indiscriminately.

1. RESOLVE CURRENT TRUTH
- Refresh repository/provider truth before branch-sensitive mutation and resolve the actual default branch, current head, overlapping work, canonical artifact registries/manifests/generators, and current outputs relevant to the request.
- Resolve the Drive side from current connected evidence. Search for the existing project/workspace and relevant files before creating folders or uploads. Reuse stable Drive file/folder identities when they exist.
- Recover relevant current-chat, handoff, plan, or artifact context yourself when accessible. Do not turn the user into a context courier.
- If Drive access is unavailable, permission is denied, or a required account/workspace cannot be resolved, name that exact external gate. Do not fabricate a successful sync.

2. BUILD THE RELEVANT ARTIFACT SET
Do not sync every tracked file. Start from the current use case and canonical repository evidence, then identify only durable artifacts that materially help the work continue, be reviewed, be presented, or remain synchronized across repo and Drive. Typical candidates can include plans/specs, decision records, status reports, client-safe documents, spreadsheets, presentations, evidence packs, exports, manifests, handoff artifacts, and intentional Drive-facing reference documents.
Exclude implementation-only source trees unless the repo explicitly publishes them as artifacts. Exclude secrets, credentials, protected/private datasets, ignored local state, dependency/vendor trees, caches, build debris, temporary logs, and anything the repository marks non-shareable.

3. CLASSIFY AUTHORITY BEFORE COPYING
For every candidate artifact assign one explicit disposition and direction:
- REPO-AUTHORITATIVE — repository canonical source may publish/update the Drive counterpart; Drive edits do not silently flow back.
- DRIVE-AUTHORITATIVE — Drive document is canonical for its content; repository may consume an intentional export/reference only when the repo contract permits it.
- BIDIRECTIONAL-BY-CONTRACT — both sides may change only because an explicit conversion/merge contract defines how conflicts and lossless round-trips work.
- DERIVED / PUBLISH-ONLY — generated or presentation artifact flows from its canonical producer to Drive and must not become a competing editable source.
- PRIVATE / DO-NOT-SYNC — artifact is intentionally excluded.
If authority cannot be determined from repository/user evidence, mark it UNKNOWN/CONFLICT and do not choose a winner by recency alone.

4. MAP IDENTITIES, NOT JUST FILENAMES
Build a compact sync map for relevant artifacts. Track, when available and safe to retain: repository canonical path or registered artifact identity; Drive file/folder identity or stable link/location; authority class; format; last proven source version/hash/timestamp; last proven Drive version/modified identity; and intended action.
Prefer stable Drive IDs/links or existing explicit mappings over name-only matching. Detect ambiguous same-name files rather than creating another copy. Do not persist sensitive Drive identifiers into the repository when repo policy says the mapping belongs in a private report or external workspace.

5. PRESERVE FORMAT AUTHORITY
Do not casually round-trip Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides through lossy exported formats and then call the result synchronized. Likewise, do not let an exported Drive copy replace a repository-native canonical source merely because it is newer.
- Preserve Google-native authority when the Drive document is the owner.
- Preserve repository-native authority when Markdown, source workbook, presentation source, structured data, or generated artifact is the owner.
- Use export/import only when an explicit conversion contract defines the accepted format and fidelity boundary.
- A PDF or rendered export is usually a publication artifact, not an editable canonical source, unless the active repository says otherwise.

6. PLAN THE SYNC LEDGER
For each relevant artifact record one action: UPLOAD, UPDATE DRIVE, DOWNLOAD/IMPORT, UPDATE REPO, NO CHANGE, CONFLICT, or SKIP. Include the reason and authority.
A useful receipt row contains:
artifact | repo identity | Drive identity/location | authority | pre-sync evidence | action | post-sync evidence | status/gate
Every material candidate must appear once. A blanket `Drive synced` statement without per-artifact accounting is invalid.

7. EXECUTE SAFE, IDEMPOTENT ACTIONS
- Reuse the existing Drive project folder and existing mapped file whenever evidence supports the identity.
- Update in place when the mapping and authority are clear; do not create `copy`, `(1)`, dated duplicate, or new project folder merely because a write is easier than resolving identity.
- Preserve repo-native canonical paths and repository artifact contracts. Do not use Drive as source control.
- When Drive-authoritative content must enter the repo, use the repository's approved import/conversion path and normal branch/validation/integration rules.
- When repo-authoritative content goes to Drive, publish the exact validated artifact or canonical source representation required by its contract.
- Do not delete, rename, move, change ownership, or broaden sharing of existing Drive content unless current evidence explicitly authorizes that destructive or access-changing action.

8. FAIL CLOSED ON TWO-SIDED DIVERGENCE
Before overwriting a mapped item, determine whether both sides materially changed since their last common/proven state when evidence permits. If both changed and no deterministic merge/precedence contract resolves the difference, classify CONFLICT. Preserve both current truths, identify the competing versions, and state the smallest user decision or owning merge mechanism required.
Timestamp-newer alone is not a safe conflict resolver. Missing comparison evidence lowers the proof ceiling; it does not authorize overwrite.

9. READ BACK AND VERIFY
After every write:
- Drive write: re-list or read the target and verify the intended existing identity, content/version/metadata relevant to the action, and workspace location.
- Repository write: verify the canonical file/artifact at the exact branch/head, run the owning focused validator/build when applicable, and integrate authorized green work according to repository policy.
- Generated artifact: verify it was produced from the current canonical generator/input floor before publishing it.
Do not infer success from a write call alone.

10. SECOND PASS TO A BOUNDED FIXED POINT
Re-scan the relevant repo artifacts and Drive workspace from the opposite direction. Catch missed renamed/moved files, stale exports, duplicate candidates, one-sided updates, newly surfaced conflicts, or artifacts that should be SKIP/PRIVATE. Execute newly safe deterministic actions, then read back again. Stop only when every in-scope artifact is CURRENT/NO CHANGE, safely synchronized, explicitly SKIPPED, CONFLICTED, or blocked by an exact external gate.

BOUNDARIES WITH SPECIALIZED WORKFLOWS
This prompt owns generic repository↔Google Drive artifact synchronization. It does not absorb project-specific management, billing, roster, taxonomy, evidence-language, or reporting semantics merely because those projects also use Drive. If the active repository has a specialized synchronizer with stronger domain rules, preserve that owner's domain authority and use this prompt only for the generic mapping/sync mechanics that remain applicable.

FINAL REPORT
Report the active repository/default branch and exact repo proof level; Drive workspace used; artifact count and per-status summary; files/folders reused versus created; repo-authoritative/Drive-authoritative/bidirectional/derived/private counts; uploads/updates/imports/no-change/conflicts/skips; focused validation and readback proof; commit/PR/merge state for repository mutation; unresolved conflicts/privacy/access gates; proof ceiling; and the first executable next action. Do not expose secrets or unnecessary private Drive identifiers in the response.
